subject: Stockwell AI - throughput chokepoint & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Asha Naik <asha@stockwell.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Jimenez <carlos.jimenez@stockwell.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: sudden p95/p99 spike on Hosted API (US) impacting inference throughput

Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp regression in response times this morning around 08:50 PST across our Stockwell integration. p95 has moved from ~220ms to ~1.2s and p99 is in the 2.5–3s range for text-generation routes. Error rate also climbed to ~4.6% (mostly 502/504). This is hitting our search pipeline and causing timeouts in our end-user flows.

We've attached a small sample of request traces and MRTG dumps (stockwell_mrtg-logs.zip). Key observations from our side:
- Spike is concentrated on /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints routed to hosted model rwd-small-v2 in us-west.
- Throughput hasn't materially increased on our side; this looks like backlog/queueing on your layer.

Can you confirm whether this is localized to a routing pool or a broader Hosted API behavior? We need an ETA and a mitigation plan — this is impacting a live control group for a launch next week.

Thanks,
Asha
Customer Success Manager
Stockwell AI

Attachments: stockwell_mrtg-logs.zip (6 files, log stubs)

Asha — thank you for the heads up and for the logs. We're on it.

Immediate next steps (internal & customer-facing):
- Internal triage: Marissa will lead RCA and loop in infra (Sean) and serving runtime (Markus).
- Temporary mitigation: can we schedule a 15-min bridge at 09:40 PST to confirm impact and implement a config flip if needed?
- I'll own communications with Stockwell and will provide rolling updates every 30 minutes until resolved.

Carlos — please keep sample traces coming if you see new failures. We'll correlate with our request logs.

On the bridge we will:
1) confirm whether backlog is due to batching/queue accumulation versus autoscaler churn or a kernel-level regression,
2) test a quick throttle to cap per-tenant concurrency, and
3) if safe, reduce the accumulation window for continuous batching (hotfix) to reduce full-batch latency.

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Success — Hosted
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Naik <asha@stockwell.ai>, Carlos Jimenez <carlos.jimenez@stockwell.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Nov 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden p95/p99 spike on Hosted API (US) impacting inference throughput — initial RCA + mitigation steps

Summary of findings so far (quick RCA):
- Root cause: Under low-to-medium concurrency the continuous-batching policy we recently rolled (commit 9f3b2) can let the batch accumulation timer drift when kernel CPU bursts delay dispatcher threads. That resulted in oversized batches for some request shapes, longer KV-cache warmup per request, and a buildup of inflight requests queued in the per-pool scheduler. In short: queue depth grew, batch sizes ballooned, and p95/p99 spiked.
- Evidence:
  * Correlated spikes in our request queue length and average batch size from 08:49–09:03 PST (see Grafana link).
  * Traces in stockwell_mrtg-logs.zip show a cluster of requests waiting >700ms before dispatch.
  * No significant upstream traffic surge from Stockwell's side.

Immediate mitigations implemented (10:02 PST):
1) Reduced continuous-batching accumulation window from 6ms -> 2ms for the affected us-west pool (hotfix toggle). This reduces max wait to avoid building large batches when dispatch is delayed.
2) Enabled per-tenant concurrency cap for Stockwell (limit 120 concurrent threads) to bound queue depth while we stabilize.
3) Bumped autoscaler cooldown to avoid oscillation-driven churn while backlog clears.

Observed impact (10:15 PST): p95 improved from ~1.2s -> ~340ms and p99 is down to ~720ms; error rate trending back below 1%. I'll keep monitoring for the next 2 hours.

Next actions (T+1–T+24 hours):
- Short term (today): roll back commit 9f3b2 on canary if further regressions appear, validate hotfix across all hosted pools, and run targeted load tests that emulate Stockwell request shapes.
- Medium term (week): add jitter guard to the batching dispatcher, add a maximum batch-size hard cap per model, and create a per-tenant watchdog that refuses requests if queue depth > threshold to provide graceful degradation.

Attachments: brief logs attached and pointers to dashboards.

Marissa Cole
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 09 Nov 2028 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-mortem and customer offer: Stockwell incident (11/09) — summary + next steps

Asha / Carlos — thank you again for your patience while we investigated. Below is a summary we shared internally and the immediate customer proposal.

What happened (TL;DR):
- A recent change to the continuous-batching dispatcher allowed batch accumulation to drift during CPU dispatch delays. That produced occasional oversized batches and a growing queue depth in the us-west hosted pool, which manifested as elevated p95/p99 and a temporary increase in 502/504 errors for Stockwell's traffic.

What we did:
- Hotfix applied (reduced accumulation window) and per-tenant concurrency cap enabled.
- Autoscaler cooldown increased to avoid churn while backlog cleared.
- We ran targeted replay tests against a Stockwell-like workload and observed p95 within normal bounds.

Customer proposal (for your approval):
- Immediate: one full week of credits on your hosted usage for the period 2028-11-09 while we complete follow-up actions.
- Next 7 days: we will run a joint validation window with Stockwell traffic and provide daily status notes.
- Follow-ups: technical fixes (dispatcher jitter guard + batch size cap) will be prioritized on our next patch across hosted pools; we will share the timeline by EOD Monday.

Requested action: Please confirm whether Stockwell accepts the week credit and whether you want Redwood to schedule a joint validation test tomorrow morning at 09:00 PST.

Thanks — we'll continue to monitor and will escalate immediately if anything else occurs.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Success — Hosted
Redwood Inference
